items.item_text: A minimum of 3 years current neonatal critical care experience required
Demonstrates ability to assess/interpret age-specific data as it pertains to the treatments administered.

Delivers age appropriate care with regards to: - Fluid and electrolytes. Assesses fluid balance in relation to providing respiratory care - Pain identification and recognizing need for pain control and intervention in order to provide treatments as ordered. - Psychosocial: Recognized age appropriate behavior for pain, separation, change in environment in relation to providing respiratory care - Growth and development: Identifies age related developmental characteristics cardiac and respiratory systems as they relate to providing respiratory care - Family/significant other involvement: Recognizes the patient's needs for family/significant other for involvement as they relate to providing respiratory care.
Encourages involvement of patient/family/significant other in decision making related to the delivery of respiratory care.

Conducts prescribed therapeutic procedures to achieve removal of broncho-pulmonary secretions and administers prescribed pharmacological agents in accordance with respiratory policies and procedures and physician orders. - Performs postural drainage and percussion as set by policy and procedure. - Performs all bronchodilator therapy via HHN, IPPB as per policy and procedure.
Conducts prescribed therapeutic procedures to achieve adequate artificial and spontaneous ventilation consistent with respiratory policies and procedures and physician orders.

Evaluates and monitors patient response to therapy. - Documents obvious signs and symptoms that indicate actual or potential problems. - Incorporates basic lab and radiological data into assessment. - Recognizes immediate life- threatening situations and seeks appropriate assistance. - Records all therapies and results as required by patient care policies and procedures.
